The rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a rich, rustic red-orange tomato sauce, infused with oregano and garlic. Tender, seared chicken breast, cut into thick chunks, is nestled amidst the pasta and sauce. Diced red bell peppers and onions are visible within the sauce, adding vibrant color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped oregano leaves garnishes the dish, providing a contrasting green. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top. The overall presentation is inviting and abundant, with moderate negative space. A folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish as the focal point with a soft, blurred background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a light-bodied Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce and chicken. Toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped oregano or basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Mozzarella Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Tomato and Mozzarella Salad is casually arranged on a simple, white ceramic plate with a slight imperfection, set on a well-used wooden dining table. Thick slices of ripe red tomatoes are interspersed with irregularly torn pieces of creamy white fresh mozzarella. Bright green basil leaves are scattered generously over the top, their vibrant color contrasting with the red and white. A glistening drizzle of dark balsamic vinegar and golden extra virgin olive oil coats the ingredients. The components are naturally overlapping, filling the plate without overcrowding, showcasing their fresh textures. A standard fork rests beside the plate on a casually placed cloth napkin. The background is a relaxed family dining area with a lived-in atmosphere, suggesting a comforting home meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an antipasto or a light lunch.
Best enjoyed with fresh, crusty bread to soak up the olive oil and tomato juices.
instructions: Wash tomatoes. Slice medium tomatoes into thick rounds. If using cherry tomatoes, halve them.
Drain mozzarella. Tear or slice mozzarella into irregular pieces.
Arrange tomato slices and mozzarella pieces casually on a serving plate. Allow them to overlap.
Scatter fresh basil leaves generously over the tomatoes and mozzarella.
Drizzle extra virgin olive oil evenly over the salad.
Drizzle balsamic vinegar over the salad.
Season generously with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper.
notes: Use the ripest, freshest tomatoes available for the best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Caprese Stuffed Chicken Breast
recipes.visual_description: A single seared and baked chicken breast is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is plump and golden-brown, with a crispy exterior. A slight opening reveals the vibrant filling of melted white mozzarella, bright red halved cherry tomatoes, and scattered fresh green basil leaves. The chicken is presented whole, showcasing its cooked form. A thin drizzle of dark balsamic glaze elegantly garnishes the chicken. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish with a soft glow. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere, keeping the focus entirely on the inviting, perfectly cooked chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple side of pasta tossed in olive oil and garlic
Accompany with a fresh green salad with a light vinaigrette
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Butterfly each chicken breast by slicing horizontally almost all the way through, creating a pocket.
Season chicken inside and out with salt and pepper.
Dice fresh mozzarella into 1cm cubes. Halve cherry tomatoes. Roughly chop fresh basil. Mince garlic.
In a small bowl, combine mozzarella, tomatoes, basil, and minced garlic. Stir gently.
Carefully stuff each chicken pocket with the mozzarella and tomato mixture. Use toothpicks to secure openings if needed.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe frying pan over medium-high heat.
Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Drizzle with balsamic glaze before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not overstuff the chicken breasts to prevent filling from leaking out during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Brazilian Lemon and Pea Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Brazilian Lemon and Pea Cream is presented in a clear, footed glass dessert bowl, showcasing its distinct layers. The bottom layer is a light brown, crumbly biscuit crust. Above it rests a creamy, pale yellow lemon layer, followed by a vibrant, smooth, light green pea puree layer, and topped with more pale yellow lemon cream. A subtle drizzle of reduced white wine creates delicate swirls on the surface. The texture appears smooth and inviting, with the biscuit base providing contrast. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections is placed next to it. A casually folded, floral-patterned chita fabric napkin is nearby. Warm, soft light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing on the dessert as the main subject.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve well-chilled after a substantial family meal.
Often accompanied by a small cup of strong, freshly brewed Brazilian coffee.

ingredients.name: Maria biscuits (or similar plain sweet biscuits)

instructions: Combine crushed Maria biscuits and melted butter. Press firmly into the bottom of four individual clear glass dessert bowls. Chill.
Pour white wine into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until only about 2 tablespoons remain. Let cool.
In a large bowl, whisk sweetened condensed milk, heavy cream, and fresh lemon juice until thick. Stir in lemon zest. Set aside.

Boil green peas in lightly salted water for 3-4 minutes until tender. Drain well. Immediately blend peas with sugar and 2 tablespoons of water until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve if desired for extra smoothness. Let cool completely.
Divide half of the lemon cream among the chilled biscuit bases.
Carefully spoon the pea puree over the lemon cream layer.
Top with the remaining lemon cream. Drizzle the cooled white wine reduction over the top of each dessert.
Chill desserts for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until firm.
notes: Ensure all components are thoroughly chilled before assembly for best results.
The pea layer provides a subtle earthy sweetness and vibrant color, not a dominant savory flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken Croquettes with Garlic Aioli
recipes.visual_description: The Spanish Chicken Croquettes are presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, embodying a refined yet approachable bistro style. Three to four golden-brown, elongated oval croquettes are neatly arranged in a slight curve or diagonal across the plate. Their exterior is visibly crisp and textured from the breadcrumb coating, with a rich, uniform golden hue. A small, elegant swirl or dollop of pale yellow garlic aioli sits beside the croquettes, offering a creamy contrast. A light dusting of smoked paprika or a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley may subtly garnish the aioli or croquettes for a touch of color. The croquettes, when cut open, reveal a creamy, off-white interior flecked with tender, shredded chicken. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded cotton napkin and a polished fork are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting from the side, casting gentle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a selection of "tapas" or small plates.
Offer with additional lemon wedges for fresh acidity.
Pair with a dry sherry (Jerez) or a light-bodied Spanish white wine.
instructions: Prepare béchamel base: Melt butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Stir in 60g plain flour. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in warm milk until mixture is smooth and thick. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until very thick and pulling away from the sides of the pan.
Remove from heat. Stir in shredded cooked chicken, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Spread mixture onto a shallow dish. Cover with cling film, pressing directly onto surface. Chill for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until firm.
Prepare breading station: Place 50g plain flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in another, and breadcrumbs in a third.
Shape croquettes: Take about 25g of chilled mixture per croquette. Form into small cylinders or oval shapes.
Coat croquettes: Roll each croquette in flour, then dip in beaten egg, then roll generously in breadcrumbs. Ensure full coating.
Heat oil: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 175°C.
Fry croquettes: Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Drain: Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Place on paper towels to drain excess oil.
Make aioli: In a small bowl, whisk egg yolk, minced garlic, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt.
Slowly drizzle in olive oil while continuously whisking until a thick, emulsified aioli forms.
Serve: Serve croquettes hot with garlic aioli on the side.
notes: Ensure the croquette mixture is thoroughly chilled for easier shaping.
Maintain oil temperature for even frying and golden crust.
traditional_techniques: Making a classic béchamel sauce (for the croquette base)

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Beet Mousse Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Chocolate Beet Mousse Cake is presented on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed with moderate negative space. The cake slice reveals distinct, clean layers: a thin, dark chocolate biscuit base, followed by a vibrant, smooth magenta beet mousse layer, topped with a rich, dark chocolate mousse layer, all encased in a glossy, reflective dark chocolate mirror glaze. The mousse layers are impeccably smooth with a creamy texture, contrasting with the slightly firm biscuit. Garnishes are minimal and precise: a cluster of bright red fresh raspberries and two small, irregular dark chocolate shards are placed delicately on top, providing color contrast and subtle height. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a single polished silver dessert fork and spoon positioned to the right. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its clean lines and appealing textures against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Roast beets: Preheat oven to 180°C. Wash beets. Wrap in foil. Roast until tender, about 45-60 minutes. Cool. Peel beets. Puree until smooth. Set aside 100g puree.

Make chocolate biscuit base: Melt 50g dark chocolate with 50g butter. Whisk 2 egg yolks with 50g sugar until pale. Fold in melted chocolate mixture. Sift in 30g flour and 15g cocoa powder. Mix until just combined. Spread thinly onto a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Bake 10-12 minutes. Cool. Cut into a 15 cm circle or desired shape. Place in a cake ring on a serving plate.

Prepare beet mousse: Soak 3g gelatin leaves in cold water. In a saucepan, combine 100g beet puree, 50g sugar, and 30ml water. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir into warm beet mixture until dissolved. Let cool slightly. Whip 200ml heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold beet mixture into whipped cream. Pour over chocolate biscuit base in the cake ring. Chill 30 minutes to set.

Prepare chocolate mousse: Soak remaining 3g gelatin leaves in cold water. Melt remaining 150g dark chocolate. In a saucepan, combine remaining 50g sugar and 30ml water. Heat until sugar dissolves. Add 1 egg yolk. Whisk constantly over low heat until mixture thickens slightly (do not boil). Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir into warm egg mixture until dissolved. Stir in melted chocolate. Let cool slightly. Whip remaining 200ml heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold chocolate mixture into whipped cream. Pour over beet mousse layer. Smooth top. Chill at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until firm.

Make chocolate mirror glaze: In a small saucepan, combine 50g dark chocolate, 30g glucose syrup, and 30ml water. Heat gently, stirring, until chocolate is melted and mixture is smooth. Remove from heat. Let cool to 30-35°C (lukewarm).

Glaze cake: Carefully remove cake from cake ring. Place on a wire rack over a baking tray. Pour lukewarm glaze evenly over cake, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off. Transfer cake to a clean serving plate.
Garnish: Arrange fresh raspberries artfully on top of the cake. Add a few small, thin chocolate shards for texture and height. Serve chilled.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Herb Gravy
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, skin crispy and deeply caramelized, sits centrally on an off-white ceramic plate. The chicken is cooked whole, displaying its natural form. Beside it, a modest pile of rustic roasted potato wedges, their skins slightly browned and interiors fluffy, are casually arranged. A vibrant green mound of tender-crisp blanched green beans rests nearby. A rich, savory herb gravy is generously drizzled over the chicken and potatoes, pooling slightly on the plate. A small sprig of fresh rosemary or thyme garnishes the dish. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a comforting, hearty portion. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, with warm, natural light illuminating the scene. A casually folded beige cloth napkin and simple, everyday flatware complete the homely, lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into rustic 2cm wedges. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until golden and tender.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a plate, tent with foil.
While chicken bakes, trim green beans. Blanch in boiling salted water for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.

Place skillet (with pan drippings) over medium heat on the stovetop. Add diced onion. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and chopped rosemary and thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour into the skillet. Whisk constantly for 1 minute to create a roux.

Gradually pour in chicken broth, whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until gravy thickens to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve each chicken thigh with a portion of roasted potatoes and green beans. Drizzle generously with herb gravy.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Tomatoes, Mushrooms, and Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of braised beef with tomatoes, mushrooms, and bell peppers is artfully arranged in the center of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Thick, tender chunks of rich brown braised beef are nestled among vibrant, large-diced red and green bell peppers, quartered earthy mushrooms, and soft diced onions, all coated in a glossy, deep reddish-brown tomato-based sauce. A sprinkle of freshly chopped bright green parsley provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness on top. The dish exhibits a natural, inviting presentation, showcasing the various ingredient textures and rich colors. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork and knife, and a neatly folded white cotton napkin to the left. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the food's appeal against a subtly blurred, restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside creamy mashed potatoes to soak up the rich sauce.
Offer crusty bread for dipping into the braising liquid.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4-5 cm cubes. Pat beef dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Dredge beef lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and large-diced red and green bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 7-8 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add quartered cremini mushrooms to the pot. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Return seared beef to the pot. Stir in diced canned tomatoes, beef broth, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Braise for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Banana Cinnamon Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously thick slice of Classic Banana Cinnamon Cake rests on an everyday, slightly imperfect cream-colored ceramic plate. The cake slice reveals a moist, golden-brown crumb speckled with dark banana bits. Its top crust is a rich, even golden-brown. A light dusting of powdered sugar is subtly sprinkled over the top of the slice. In the soft-focused background, the remainder of the round, rustic cake sits on a simple wire cooling rack on a well-used wooden dining table. The setting evokes a homely family kitchen with warm, natural light filtering in, highlighting the comforting texture of the cake. A casual, folded linen napkin and a simple silver fork are placed beside the plate. The overall scene is warm, inviting, and unpretentious, emphasizing the homemade quality of the dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 15 cm round cake pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together whole wheat flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, baking soda, ground cinnamon, and salt.
In a separate bowl, combine mashed bananas, egg, milk, and melted butter. Mix well.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Stir until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared cake pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes.
Invert cake onto a wire rack. Let cool completely.
Lightly dust cooled cake with powdered sugar before serving.
notes: Use very ripe bananas for the best flavor and sweetness.
Ensure butter is melted but not hot before mixing with other wet ingredients.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Banana Pancakes
recipes.visual_description: A stack of three golden-brown pancakes rests on a simple, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The pancakes are fluffy, with visible pockets. Slices of ripe banana are casually placed around the base of the pancake stack and on top. A small pat of unsalted butter, slightly melted, sits on the topmost pancake. A rich amber maple syrup is drizzled generously over the stack, glistening. The plate is centered on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple fork and a crumpled cloth napkin are nearby. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere. The overall presentation is unpretentious and comforting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Drizzle with maple syrup
Serve with fresh fruit

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter
ingredients.quantity: 30 g (for batter) plus more for cooking

instructions: Mash ripe bananas in a large bowl.
Add egg, milk, 30 g melted butter, granulated sugar, and ground cinnamon to mashed bananas. Whisk until well combined.
In a separate bowl, combine whole wheat flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add dry ingredients to the wet banana mixture. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix; lumps are fine.
Heat a large frying pan or griddle over medium heat. Lightly butter the pan.
Pour approximately 60 ml of batter per pancake onto the hot pan.
Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and bubbles form on the surface. Flip and cook until cooked through.
Repeat with remaining batter, adding more butter to the pan as needed.
Serve pancakes warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Apple Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of classic apple crumble served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with subtle rim imperfections. The topping is a rugged, golden-brown crust featuring coarse flour crumbs and toasted rolled oats. Soft, 2cm chunks of stewed Granny Smith apples are visible beneath the topping, with thick, caramelized amber juices bubbling slightly at the dish's edges. A single, generous pour of thick, pale yellow vanilla custard pools naturally on one side, partially melting into the warm crumble. The bowl sits on a dark, weathered oak table beside a folded linen napkin and a tarnished silver spoon. Soft, warm kitchen light emphasizes the crunchy textures and steam rising from the fruit.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with hot vanilla custard
Accompany with a dollop of clotted cream
Pair with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel, core, and cut apples into 2cm chunks.
Toss apples with 50g sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Transfer apple mixture to a 20cm baking dish.
Cut cold butter into small cubes.
Rub butter into flour using fingertips until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Stir in remaining 100g sugar and rolled oats.
Spread crumble topping evenly over the apples.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden brown and fruit is bubbling.
Remove from oven and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use cold butter to ensure a crisp, crumbly texture.
Do not overwork the dough or it will become tough.
Granny Smith apples provide the best tart balance to the sweet topping.

recipes.recipe_name: Pineapple Coconut Chicken Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Pineapple Coconut Chicken Curry is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl, placed on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. Steamed white jasmine rice forms a base, generously topped with the vibrant, creamy curry. The sauce is a warm yellow-orange hue, flecked with small, soft pieces of caramelized onion, garlic, and ginger. Succulent 3 cm chunks of chicken breast are visible, simmered until tender. Bright 2 cm chunks of pineapple are nestled throughout, offering a contrasting sweet-tart note and adding pops of golden color. A light scattering of fresh chopped cilantro adds a touch of green. The overall impression is hearty, comforting, and visually inviting, typical of a home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a side of fresh lime wedges for squeezing.
Serve with a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Fresh pineapple
ingredients.quantity: 300 g, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Cook jasmine rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in curry powder and chili flakes. Cook for 30 seconds.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear chicken until lightly browned on all sides. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Pour in coconut milk. Add fish sauce, salt, and black pepper. Stir well.
Bring the curry to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in pineapple chunks. Cook for another 5 minutes, allowing pineapple to heat through and slightly soften.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot over cooked jasmine rice. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: For a spicier curry, increase red chili flakes or add a fresh chopped chili with the aromatics.
Chicken thighs can be used instead of breast for a richer flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Lamb Croquettes with Garlic Aioli
recipes.visual_description: Three golden-brown, elongated oval croquettes are artfully arranged on a clean white porcelain plate, slightly off-center to allow for negative space. Each croquette boasts a crispy, light golden-brown panko crust with subtle textural variations. A generous dollop of creamy, off-white garlic aioli sits beside the croquettes, its smooth surface contrasting with the croquettes' texture. A delicate sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley adds a vibrant green accent over the aioli and croquettes. The background features a simple wooden table surface, with a silver fork and knife placed neatly beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating a professional yet approachable presentation. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced and appealing starter portion.

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley, finely chopped, for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season lamb shoulder generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear lamb on all sides until browned. Remove lamb.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add crushed garlic, bay leaf, and thyme. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return lamb to the pot. Pour in beer and beef stock.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Cover pot tightly. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise 2.5 to 3 hours, or until lamb is fork-tender.
Remove lamb from pot. Shred meat using two forks. Discard any large fat pieces.
Strain braising liquid into a saucepan. Discard solids. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until thickened, about 10-15 minutes. You should have about 50 ml of rich sauce.
Combine shredded lamb with 30 ml of reduced sauce. Mix well. Chill lamb mixture 1 hour until firm.
Form chilled lamb mixture into 12 elongated oval or cylindrical croquettes.
Set up a breading station: one bowl with flour, one with beaten eggs, one with panko breadcrumbs.
Dredge each croquette in flour, then egg, then panko. Ensure full coating.
For Garlic Aioli: Whisk egg yolk, minced garlic, Dijon mustard, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Slowly drizzle in olive oil while continuously whisking until aioli is thick and emulsified. Season with salt.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan to 170°C. Oil should be deep enough to submerge croquettes.
Carefully fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Serve 3 croquettes per plate with a dollop of garlic aioli. Garnish with finely chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Shoyu Ramen
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated bowl of Chicken Shoyu Ramen is centered on a simple wooden table. A deep white ceramic ramen bowl holds clear, amber broth and fresh, wavy noodles. Thick chunks of seared chicken are arranged atop the noodles. Vibrant green blanched bok choy leaves provide fresh contrast. A perfectly soft-boiled egg, halved lengthwise, reveals its jammy golden yolk. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced bright green spring onions, a dark green rectangular nori sheet, and golden-brown roasted garlic cloves. The balanced composition is inviting. Dark wooden chopsticks rest beside the bowl on a light cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately in deep ceramic ramen bowls.
Offer additional condiments like chili oil (rayu) on the side.
Use chopsticks for eating noodles and solids, a large ceramic spoon for broth.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut off the top of the whole garlic head. Drizzle with olive oil. Wrap in foil. Roast for 30-40 minutes until very soft. Squeeze out cloves. Mash half for broth, reserve half for garnish.

Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Sear in a hot pan until golden brown on both sides. Transfer seared chicken to a pot. Add 1.5 litres chicken broth, 3 smashed garlic cloves, and 30g sliced ginger. Simmer gently for 20-25 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and is tender. Remove chicken. Shred into bite-sized pieces or slice into thick chunks. Strain broth, discard aromatics. Keep broth warm.

Bring a small pot of water to a rolling boil. Gently lower 3 eggs into the boiling water. Cook for exactly 6.5 minutes. Immediately transfer eggs to an ice bath. Peel carefully. Slice each egg in half lengthwise.
In a small saucepan, combine 100ml soy sauce, 50ml water, and 1 teaspoon sugar. Bring to a simmer. Stir until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. This is your shoyu tare.
Briefly blanch 150g bok choy or spinach in the hot chicken broth for 1 minute until tender-crisp. Remove and drain.
Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Cook 270g fresh ramen noodles according to package instructions (usually 2-3 minutes). Drain well.

Divide the shoyu tare evenly among 3 large ramen bowls. Add 500ml hot chicken broth to each bowl. Stir to combine. Add a portion of cooked noodles to each bowl. Arrange shredded chicken, blanched greens, and half a soft-boiled egg in each bowl. Garnish with thinly sliced spring onions, a sheet of nori, and a few roasted garlic cloves. Drizzle with a few drops of sesame oil. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Assembling ramen bowls with specific tare and toppings

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Shoyu Noodle Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Shoyu Noodle Soup is presented in a deep, matte black ceramic ramen bowl. The clear, amber-hued broth serves as the base. Neatly arranged ramen noodles are submerged, topped with tender, thinly sliced chicken pieces. Two halves of a soft-boiled egg, revealing a vibrant golden, slightly runny yolk, are carefully placed on the side. The soup is garnished with a generous scattering of bright green scallion rounds and a delicate drizzle of sesame oil, creating a subtle sheen. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table, accompanied by a pair of elegant wooden chopsticks and a large white ceramic soup spoon. A simple folded white cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, set against a blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side dish of shichimi togarashi (Japanese seven-spice blend) for diners to add heat.
Offer a small dish of finely sliced pickled ginger as an optional palate cleanser.
Serve hot, allowing diners to slurp noodles and broth directly from the bowl.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add chicken breast. Cook for 15-20 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Let cool slightly. Shred or thinly slice chicken. Set aside.

In a separate pot, bring water to a rolling boil for eggs. Gently lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for 6-7 minutes for soft-boiled. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Peel eggs carefully. Halve each egg lengthwise.
In a large pot, combine chicken broth, minced garlic, and sliced ginger. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Strain the broth to remove garlic and ginger. Return clear broth to the pot.
Stir in soy sauce and mirin. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt if needed. Keep warm.
Cook ramen noodles according to package instructions in a separate pot of boiling water. Drain well.
Divide cooked noodles evenly among 3 deep soup bowls.
Arrange shredded or sliced chicken over the noodles in each bowl.
Carefully ladle hot broth over noodles and chicken.
Place two egg halves on top of the chicken and noodles in each bowl.
Drizzle each bowl with sesame oil. Garnish generously with sliced green onions. Serve immediately.
notes: Achieving the perfect soft-boiled egg is key to this dish. Adjust cooking time based on egg size and desired yolk consistency.
The broth can be prepared in advance for quicker assembly.
For richer flavor, use chicken thighs instead of breast.

recipes.recipe_name: Homely Chicken & Egg Ramen
recipes.special_requests: non-alcohol, have a chicken fillet, don't have cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Homely Chicken & Egg Ramen is presented in a deep, wide ceramic bowl, evoking a sense of warmth and comfort. The golden-brown, subtly creamy broth forms the inviting base, with a hearty tangle of cooked ramen noodles submerged. Tender, irregular chunks of shredded chicken are scattered generously over the noodles. Bright orange, thinly sliced carrot rounds are interspersed, adding a pop of color and gentle crunch. One perfectly soft-boiled egg, halved lengthwise, rests prominently on the noodles, its vibrant yellow yolk peeking out. A small, rustic dollop of Dijon mustard is placed on the bowl's rim, ready to be mixed in. The dish is finished with a sprinkle of thinly sliced green onions, adding a fresh, verdant touch. It sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, inviting light. Simple, everyday chopsticks rest casually alongside the bowl, completing the homely, authentic scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks
Use deep ceramic ramen bowls
instructions: Prepare Chicken: Place chicken fillet in a saucepan. Cover with water. Bring to a simmer. Cook 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Shred into irregular chunks using two forks. Set aside.

Cook Eggs: While chicken cooks, bring a separate small pot of water to a boil. Gently lower eggs into boiling water. Cook 6-7 minutes for soft-boiled. Transfer to an ice bath. Peel carefully. Halve lengthwise.

Make Broth: In a large pot, heat sesame oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in chicken broth and soy sauce. Bring to a simmer. Whisk in mayonnaise until fully combined and broth is slightly creamy. Add thinly sliced carrot rounds. Simmer 5-7 minutes until carrots are tender-crisp.
Cook Noodles: In a separate pot, cook ramen noodles according to package directions. Drain well.
Assemble Soup: Divide cooked noodles among 3 deep ceramic bowls. Ladle hot broth and carrots over noodles. Arrange shredded chicken chunks on top. Place 2 egg halves per bowl.
Garnish and Serve: Sprinkle generously with thinly sliced green onions. Add a small dollop of Dijon mustard to the side of the bowl if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken & Egg Ramen Stir-fry
recipes.special_requests: non-alcohol, have a chicken fillet, don't have cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single modest portion of the stir-fry is served in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The noodles are loosely piled, intertwined with golden-brown chicken chunks, vibrant orange julienned carrots, and soft yellow scrambled egg pieces. A scattering of bright green chopped spring onions adds a pop of color on top. The components are naturally mixed and slightly overlapping, reflecting a comforting, home-style meal. No strict arrangement, just a generous scoop. The bowl rests on a well-used, slightly worn light wooden dining table. Beside the bowl, a pair of simple wooden chopsticks are casually placed on a small, plain ceramic rest. A folded, light-colored cloth napkin is tucked under the bowl. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a warm, inviting kitchen environment. Warm, soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing the textures and creating subtle shadows. Chicken is cut into bite-sized chunks. Carrots are julienned into thin strips. Eggs are scrambled into soft, irregular pieces.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled ginger.
Offer a small bowl of chili oil for those who prefer extra heat.
instructions: Prepare ingredients: Cut chicken into 2cm chunks. Julienne carrot into thin strips. Mince garlic. Grate ginger.
Cook ramen: Boil 1.5 litres of water in a pot. Add ramen noodles. Cook for 3 minutes until al dente. Drain well.

Cook chicken: Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Cook eggs: Add remaining 5ml oil to the same pan. Beat eggs in a small bowl. Pour in beaten eggs. Scramble until just set. Remove eggs from pan. Set aside.

Stir-fry vegetables: Add remaining 10ml vegetable oil to the pan. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add julienned carrot. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Make sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mayonnaise, and mustard.
Combine: Return cooked ramen, chicken, and scrambled egg to the pan with carrots. Pour in the sauce. Toss well to coat all ingredients evenly.
Finish: Stir-fry briefly for 1 minute until heated through. Drizzle with sesame oil if desired.
Serve: Transfer to individual bowls. Garnish with chopped spring onions.
notes: This dish is best served immediately.
Adjust mustard quantity to your preferred level of tanginess.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken with Root Vegetables
recipes.special_requests: European cuisine, non-alcohol, have a chicken fillet, don't have cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken fillet is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Rustic large chunks of fork-tender potatoes and thick slices of vibrant orange carrots are artfully arranged around the chicken. The chicken and vegetables are generously coated in a rich, rustic red tomato and oregano sauce, with visible pieces of caramelized onion and minced garlic. The chicken boasts a golden-brown exterior from initial searing, contrasting with its tender interior. Vegetables retain their shape and bright color. A fresh sprig of oregano rests atop the chicken, with a slight drizzle of golden olive oil enhancing the sheen. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, and natural, even lighting from the side, creating a warm bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread to soak up the rich sauce.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken fillets with salt and pepper. Sear chicken 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Add bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken fillets to the pot. Add potato chunks and carrot slices around the chicken.
Cover the pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and vegetables are fork-tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with a fresh oregano sprig.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Root Vegetables
recipes.special_requests: European cuisine, non-alcohol, have a chicken fillet, don't have cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, comforting baked chicken and root vegetables. A single generous portion rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table. Chicken chunks are nestled among roasted potato chunks, carrot rounds, and onion quarters. The chicken is golden-brown, with tender white meat. Potatoes are soft, browned at edges. Carrots are vibrant orange. Onions are caramelized. Roasted tomatoes create a rich sauce coating ingredients. Fresh, chopped parsley adds color. Warm kitchen light creates soft shadows. A simple glass of water and a casually folded cloth napkin complete the homely kitchen scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking dish onto individual plates.
Best served with crusty bread for dipping in the savory sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and peel potatoes and carrots. Cut potatoes into 3 cm chunks. Cut carrots into 2 cm thick rounds.
Peel and quarter the onion. Peel and mince garlic cloves.
Pat chicken fillets dry. Cut each fillet into 2-3 large chunks.
In a large roasting dish, combine potato chunks, carrot rounds, onion quarters, minced garlic, diced tomatoes, dried oregano, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix well to coat all vegetables.
Nestle chicken chunks among the vegetables. Pour chicken broth into the dish.
Bake for 35-40 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature. It should reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Paella
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Chicken Paella is presented on a round, shallow, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rice is a vibrant golden-yellow, spread evenly across the plate. Two to three golden-brown, seared chicken thigh pieces are nestled into the rice, skin side up. The chicken pieces are whole, succulent, and not sliced. Diced red and green bell peppers are visible throughout the rice, adding bright flecks of color. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is scattered over the top. Two bright yellow lemon wedges are placed thoughtfully on the side of the plate. The rice appears moist and tender, with a subtle hint of caramelized 'socarrat' texture on the bottom. The chicken skin is crispy, contrasting with the tender meat. The dominant color is golden-yellow from the saffron rice, complemented by the rich brown chicken, bright red and green peppers, and vibrant green parsley. The paella occupies the central two-thirds of the plate, leaving a clean white rim. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface. A clean white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, with natural, even lighting highlighting the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the paella pan for a communal experience, or individually plated.
Offer extra lemon wedges on the side for squeezing over the dish.
Accompany with crusty bread to soak up any remaining juices.

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, diced into 2 cm pieces
Green bell pepper, diced into 2 cm pieces
Ripe tomatoes, grated or finely diced
Saffron threads, steeped in 60 ml hot water

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 pieces each. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced red and green bell peppers. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften.
Stir in grated tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing moisture to evaporate.
Add smoked paprika and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat rice grains with the sofrito mixture for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in hot chicken broth and the steeped saffron liquid. Stir gently to distribute ingredients. Bring to a boil.
Arrange the seared chicken pieces evenly over the rice. Do not stir the rice after this point.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is al dente. A crispy crust (socarrat) should form on the bottom.
If liquid evaporates too quickly, add a small amount more hot broth, but avoid over-wetting. Do not stir.
Remove from heat. Cover the paella pan with foil or a clean kitchen towel. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.
traditional_techniques: Socarrat (caramelized rice crust at the bottom of the pan)

recipes.recipe_name: Hand-Rolled Potato Gnocchi with Brown Butter Sage
recipes.visual_description: The Hand-Rolled Potato Gnocchi with Brown Butter Sage presents as a warm, inviting main course on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The gnocchi pieces are plump, irregularly shaped, and golden-brown from the butter, with visible ridges. They are tossed generously in a glistening, fluid brown butter sauce, pooling slightly. Crispy, deep green sage leaves are scattered throughout, providing vibrant color contrast. A generous dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese tops the dish, melting slightly. A few cracks of fresh black pepper enhance texture. The composition is organic, flowing, with moderate negative space. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and golden tones.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Offer crusty artisan bread to soak up the leftover sauce.
Pair with a light-bodied Italian white wine or a sparkling water.
instructions: Wash potatoes. Boil or steam whole potatoes in their skins until very tender. Drain well.
Peel hot potatoes. Pass them through a potato ricer or mash thoroughly. Ensure no lumps remain. Spread riced potato on a clean surface to cool slightly.

Create a well in the center of the riced potatoes. Add flour, egg yolk, and salt to the well. Gently mix with a fork, incorporating potato from the sides. Knead briefly and lightly until a soft, cohesive dough forms. Do not over-knead.
Divide dough into four portions. Roll each portion into a long rope, approximately 2 cm thick, on a lightly floured surface. Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces.
Gently roll each piece over the tines of a fork or a gnocchi board to create ridges.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add gnocchi in batches. Cook until gnocchi float to the surface, typically 1-2 minutes. Let them float for 15-30 seconds more. Remove with a slotted spoon.
While gnocchi cook, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add sage leaves. Cook until butter browns and sage leaves are crispy. Be careful not to burn.
Add cooked gnocchi directly to the skillet with the brown butter sage sauce. Toss gently to coat.
Plate immediately. Garnish with fresh Parmigiano-Reggiano and a grind of black pepper.
notes: Use starchy potatoes for best gnocchi texture.
Avoid overworking the gnocchi dough; it will become tough.
Do not overcrowd the pot when boiling gnocchi; cook in batches.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Chicken Soba Stir-Fry
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Savory Chicken Soba Stir-Fry rests in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The soba noodles, dark brown and slightly glossy from the sauce, are loosely piled. Tender, pan-fried chicken chunks, golden-brown and irregular in shape, are nestled among the noodles. Vibrant, crisp-tender vegetables – thin julienned carrot strips, bright red bell pepper slices, and whole green snap peas – are mixed throughout, adding bursts of color and texture. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds and thinly sliced green spring onion tops. The bowl sits directly on the wooden table, alongside a pair of natural wooden chopsticks and a small, simple ceramic soy sauce dish. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting appeal of the home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Provide wooden chopsticks for eating.
Offer a small side dish of pickled ginger or shichimi togarashi for extra flavor.
instructions: Cut chicken into 2 cm cubes. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Slice bell pepper into thin strips. Julienne carrots. Trim snap peas. Mince garlic. Grate ginger. Slice spring onions diagonally, separate white and green parts.
In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sake (if using), water/broth, brown sugar, and sesame oil. Set aside.
Cook soba noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Drain again.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Cook until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet.

Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the skillet. Add white parts of spring onions, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add carrots and bell pepper. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender. Add snap peas and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet with vegetables. Add cooked soba noodles. Stir the sauce mixture, then pour over the noodles, chicken, and vegetables.
Bring to a simmer. In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 2 tbsp water to make a slurry. Add slurry to the skillet. Stir constantly until sauce thickens and coats ingredients.
Transfer to serving bowls. Garnish with green parts of spring onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve hot.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents seared boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into generous 5cm chunks, coated in a rich, creamy sauce. The golden-brown chicken pieces are nestled amongst vibrant green wilted spinach and ruby-red sun-dried tomato halves. The sauce, a harmonious blend of cream and Parmesan, gently clings to all components, showcasing a velvety texture. Garnished with fresh chopped Italian parsley, the dish offers a delightful contrast of colors and textures. It is served in a clean, white porcelain dinner plate on a simple wooden table, accompanied by classic Italian flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting, rustic elegance. A single portion is thoughtfully arranged with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Serve alongside a simple green salad.
Serve over pasta, such as tagliatelle or penne.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut each thigh into 2-3 large chunks (approx. 5cm pieces). Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and sliced sun-dried tomatoes to the pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Stir in heavy cream and dried oregano. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add fresh spinach to the pan. Cook until spinach is wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Return cooked chicken pieces to the pan. Toss to coat them in the creamy sauce. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Roasted Chicken with Herbed Potatoes and Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of Pan-Roasted Chicken is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. One whole, boneless, skin-on chicken thigh, boasting a deeply golden-brown and crispy skin, is the focal point. Adjacent to the chicken, a neat cluster of golden-brown roasted potato wedges is arranged. Alongside, several vibrant green asparagus spears, lightly charred, complete the main components. A rich, glossy pan sauce, infused with herbs and lemon, is artfully drizzled over the chicken and pooled at its base. The dish exhibits a natural color balance of golden browns, vibrant greens, and rich amber tones. Garnished simply with a fresh sprig of rosemary and a bright lemon wedge placed beside the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, standard silver flatware, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a relaxed restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a large oven-safe skillet, heat 30ml olive oil over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken. Sear for 2-3 minutes on other side. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to skillet. Add potato wedges. Season with salt, pepper, chopped rosemary, and chopped thyme.
Sauté potatoes for 5-7 minutes until lightly browned.
Return chicken thighs to skillet, nestling them among potatoes.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes.
After 15 minutes of roasting, add asparagus spears to skillet. Continue roasting until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and potatoes are tender.
Remove skillet from oven. Transfer chicken, potatoes, and asparagus to a serving platter. Cover loosely with foil.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove from heat. Whisk in butter until melted and sauce is slightly thickened.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice into sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Drizzle pan sauce over chicken and vegetables. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Chicken Soba Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Japanese Chicken Soba Stir-fry is casually plated on an everyday, off-white ceramic dish, resting on a well-worn wooden dining table. Seared chicken chunks, approximately 2 cm, are nestled among a mound of springy soba noodles. Vibrant julienned red bell pepper and carrots, along with bright green snap peas, are interspersed throughout, adding pops of color and texture. Fresh, thinly sliced spring onions are sprinkled over the top. The noodles and ingredients are coated in a glossy, savory sauce. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, natural kitchen light, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks.
Offer a small dish of shichimi togarashi (Japanese seven-spice blend) for optional added heat.
instructions: Cook soba noodles according to package instructions. Drain well. Rinse with cold water. Drain again.
Cut chicken thighs into 2 cm chunks. Pat dry.
Julienne red bell pepper and carrot. Trim snap peas. Thinly slice spring onions.
Grate ginger. Mince garlic.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, toasted sesame oil, grated ginger, minced garlic, and water. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep frying pan over high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add julienned bell pepper and carrot to the wok. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add snap peas and most of the sliced spring onions to the wok. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add cooked soba noodles and the prepared sauce.
Toss everything together for 1-2 minutes until ingredients are well coated and heated through.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh spring onions.
traditional_techniques: Mise en place (preparation of all ingredients before cooking)

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Beef & Mushroom Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A rustic wooden board or simple white ceramic platter holds 8-12 bite-sized Savory Beef & Mushroom Crostini. Each crostini features a golden-brown, toasted baguette slice, about 1.5 cm thick, topped generously with a hearty, dark brown mixture of minced beef, sliced mushrooms, finely diced onion, minced garlic, and diced tomatoes. The beef and mushroom mixture has a rich, savory appearance with visible textures of tender cooked beef and softened mushroom slices. Flecks of bright red from the tomato are interspersed. Each piece is garnished with a sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley. The crostini are arranged casually with some pieces touching, forming an inviting, natural cluster on the board. The setting is a homely family kitchen, with the board placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Natural, warm lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The entire platter is visible, showcasing the comfort-focused presentation.
instructions: Dice onion. Mince garlic. Slice mushrooms. Dice tomatoes.
Brown beef mince in a large pan over medium-high heat. Break up lumps. Cook until no pink remains. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pan with beef. Cook for 5 minutes until onion softens.
Stir in sliced mushrooms and diced tomatoes. Cook for 8-10 minutes until mushrooms are tender and liquid reduces. Season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Brush both sides lightly with olive oil.
Arrange baguette slices on a baking tray. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Spoon the beef and mushroom mixture generously onto each toasted baguette slice.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Garnish each crostini with chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz de Forno com Frango e Urucum
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Arroz de Forno com Frango e Urucum rests on a simple, rustic ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Tender, bone-in chicken thighs, deeply golden-brown from searing, are nestled into a bed of vibrant reddish-orange rice. The rice is infused with annatto, displaying a comforting, slightly irregular texture from the baking process. Diced red bell pepper and onion pieces are visible throughout the rice, adding flecks of color. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish. The components touch and slightly overlap, creating a natural, homely presentation. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, reflecting a relaxed family dining atmosphere. A simple glass of water and a plain fork and knife are placed beside the plate. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a hearty, inviting portion. The chicken is presented as whole pieces, not sliced or fanned.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add annatto seeds. Cook 1 minute until oil is deep orange. Discard seeds.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, in the annatto oil for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and ketchup. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add uncooked rice to the pot. Stir to combine. Nestle seared chicken thighs into the rice mixture, skin-side up.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid or foil. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake 30-35 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from oven. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Pork & Macaroni Gratin with Fermented Root Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Sustainable Pork & Macaroni Gratin rests in a handcrafted, shallow ceramic bowl with a natural, unglazed rim. The gratin features a golden-brown, crispy breadcrumb crust, revealing tender, slow-cooked pork chunks and al dente macaroni beneath, coated in a creamy, subtly spiced sauce. The pork is presented in natural, rustic chunks, not sliced. Colors are warm and inviting, primarily golden-brown and creamy beige. Beside the gratin, a small, vibrant mound of julienned fermented root vegetable slaw adds a burst of contrasting color—orange from carrots, pale yellow from parsnips, and light green from cabbage—and a fresh, crisp texture. The dish is placed on a light, reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is gently folded beside the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the organic textures of the food and serving ware. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green from a blurred plant, emphasizing the dish as the focal point.
instructions: Prepare fermented root slaw first. Thinly slice carrots, parsnips, and green cabbage into julienne strips. Combine vegetables in a clean jar.

Dissolve 1 tablespoon non-iodized salt in 500 ml water to make brine. Pour brine over vegetables in jar. Ensure vegetables are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Refrigerate once desired tanginess is achieved.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cut pork shoulder into 3 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot. Reserve.
Dice one onion. Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the pot. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Return pork to pot. Add bay leaf and thyme sprigs. Pour in 400 ml stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover pot. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise for 90-120 minutes, or until pork is fork-tender.
Remove pork from oven. Discard bay leaf and thyme. Shred pork into smaller pieces using two forks. Reserve braising liquid.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Reserve a small amount of pasta water if needed for sauce consistency.
Finely dice remaining onion. In a separate saucepan, melt 30 g butter (if using) or 1 tbsp oil. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent.
Whisk in flour to create a roux. Cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in 300 ml milk and 300 ml reserved braising liquid until smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook until sauce thickens.
Stir Dijon mustard into the sauce. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Add shredded pork and cooked macaroni to the sauce. Mix well.
Transfer pork and macaroni mixture to an oven-safe gratin dish. Top evenly with breadcrumbs.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until gratin is golden brown and bubbling. If breadcrumbs brown too quickly, cover loosely with foil.
Serve hot with a side of the fermented root slaw.

recipes.recipe_name: Peach and Tomato Glazed Chicken with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Peach and Tomato Glazed Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. A seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a slight char, rests as the focal point. Alongside the chicken, a vibrant mix of roasted butternut squash cubes, red and yellow bell pepper squares, and caramelized red onion wedges are neatly arranged. A rich, glossy peach and tomato glaze is generously spooned over the chicken, with some pooling subtly on the plate. The colors are natural and balanced: warm browns of the chicken, bright oranges and reds from the vegetables, and a deep, inviting hue from the glaze. A fresh sprig of green thyme garnishes the dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel butternut squash. Cut squash into 2cm cubes. Cut bell peppers into 2cm squares. Cut red onion into 2cm wedges. Mince garlic cloves.
Toss squash, bell peppers, onion, and minced garlic with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized. Stir halfway through.
While vegetables roast, prepare chicken. Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm.
For the glaze, dice peaches and tomatoes. Add diced peaches and tomatoes to the same skillet. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in chicken broth, apple cider vinegar, and honey. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens slightly and peaches break down.
Season glaze with salt and pepper to taste.

Plate roasted vegetables on white porcelain plates. Place one seared chicken breast beside the vegetables. Spoon peach and tomato glaze generously over chicken. Garnish each plate with a fresh thyme sprig. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Confit Egg Yolk, Prosciutto Crisp, Mozzarella Espuma
recipes.visual_description: A single, glistening, golden-orange confit egg yolk, perfectly round, is placed slightly off-center on a large, pristine, matte bone china plate. Beside the yolk, an ethereal cloud of bright white mozzarella espuma is gently piped. One or two irregularly shaped, thin, amber-colored prosciutto crisps stand upright or lean artfully against the yolk or espuma, showcasing their delicate texture. A few finely minced fresh chives are precisely sprinkled over the yolk and espuma, adding a vibrant green accent. The plate features abundant negative space. The setting is a dark, polished wooden table, with a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, directional lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing depth and highlighting the dish's sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Gently separate egg yolks. Place yolks in a small, heatproof dish. Cover completely with olive oil.
Cook in a preheated oven at 65°C (150°F) for 45-60 minutes until yolks are jammy but not firm. Carefully remove yolks from oil. Season lightly with salt.
Lay prosciutto slices on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Place another sheet of parchment and a second baking tray on top to keep them flat.
Bake in a preheated oven at 160°C (320°F) for 10-15 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Cool completely. Break into irregular, elegant pieces.
Drain mozzarella. Combine mozzarella and milk in a small saucepan. Heat gently, stirring until mozzarella melts into the milk and forms a smooth liquid. Do not boil.

Season with a pinch of salt. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into a siphon bottle (0.5L capacity). Charge with one N2O cartridge. Shake well. Keep warm in a bain-marie or use immediately.
On each large, pristine white plate, place one confit egg yolk slightly off-center.
Gently pipe a small, delicate cloud of mozzarella espuma beside the yolk.
Lean one or two crisp prosciutto pieces artfully against the yolk or espuma.
Garnish with a tiny sprinkle of finely minced chives over the yolk and espuma. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Georgian Walnut Eggplant with Pan-Seared Tofu
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Georgian Walnut Eggplant with Pan-Seared Tofu is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Roasted eggplant, cut into 2-3 cm cubes, is richly coated in a textured, earthy-brown walnut sauce, mounded loosely. Golden-brown pan-seared tofu planks, 2 cm thick, are arranged beside the eggplant, displaying a crispy exterior. A generous dollop of creamy white cucumber yogurt offers a cooling contrast. The dish is garnished with vibrant fresh cilantro leaves and a few whole walnut halves. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting features a light wooden table surface and a neatly folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights textures. The background suggests a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm Georgian bread (puri) or lavash.
Pair with a dry white Georgian wine.
instructions: Prepare Eggplant: Wash eggplants. Cut into 2-3 cm cubes or thick wedges. Place in a colander. Sprinkle generously with salt. Let sit for 30 minutes to draw out moisture. Rinse thoroughly under cold water. Pat very dry with kitchen paper.
Cook Eggplant: Heat 45ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add eggplant in batches. Cook until golden brown and tender, about 8-10 minutes per batch. Remove eggplant and set aside.
Prepare Tofu: Press 400g firm tofu to remove excess water. Cut tofu into 2 cm thick planks or 3 cm cubes. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Sear Tofu: Heat 15ml olive oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Add tofu. Sear until golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 4-5 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.

Make Walnut Sauce: In a food processor, combine 200g walnuts, 4 peeled garlic cloves, 1 small red onion (roughly chopped), 30g fresh cilantro, 20ml white wine vinegar, 5g ground coriander, 3g ground fenugreek, and 2g red chili flakes (if using). Add 15ml olive oil and 50ml water. Process until a thick, coarse paste forms. Season with salt and black pepper.
Combine Eggplant and Sauce: In a large bowl, gently toss the cooked eggplant with the walnut sauce. Ensure all eggplant pieces are well coated.

Prepare Cucumber Yogurt: Grate 1 large cucumber. Squeeze out excess water. In a small bowl, combine grated cucumber with 200g Greek yogurt and 1 minced garlic clove (optional). Season with a pinch of salt.

Serve: Arrange the walnut-coated eggplant on serving plates. Place the pan-seared tofu alongside. Serve with a dollop of cucumber yogurt on the side. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and a few whole walnut halves.
notes: This dish is inspired by Georgian 'Badrijani Nigvzit' (eggplant with walnut sauce), adapted to be a satisfying main course with tofu.
traditional_techniques: Preparation of a walnut paste (similar to Nigvzis Sakmeli)

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hungarian Chicken Paprikash is plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A succulent, golden-brown chicken thigh, braised to tender perfection, rests prominently, coated in a rich, velvety, reddish-orange paprika sauce. The sauce, thick and glossy, pools around the chicken, showcasing flecks of finely diced red bell pepper. Beside the chicken, a cluster of golden-roasted potato chunks, their skins slightly crisped, are neatly arranged. A vibrant medley of sautéed cremini mushrooms and bright yellow bell pepper julienne adds contrasting color and texture. Fresh chopped parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce. The overall presentation is warm and inviting, balancing rustic appeal with refined plating. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware, under soft, natural lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted potatoes and a side of sautéed vegetables.
Traditionally accompanied by nokedli (Hungarian dumplings) or wide egg noodles.

ingredients.name: New potatoes or small Yukon Gold, 2-3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and diced red bell pepper. Cook for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Remove pot from heat briefly. Stir in sweet paprika and hot paprika (if using) and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return pot to heat. Pour in chicken broth, scraping up browned bits. Bring to a simmer.

Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Cover and simmer gently for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
While chicken braises, preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato chunks with a drizzle of oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown.

In a separate pan, heat a small amount of oil over medium-high heat. Add quartered mushrooms and julienned yellow bell pepper. Sauté until mushrooms are golden and bell pepper is tender-crisp, 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Remove chicken from pot. In a small bowl, whisk together sour cream and flour until smooth. Gradually whisk a ladleful of hot sauce from the pot into the sour cream mixture to temper it. Pour tempered sour cream mixture back into the pot, stirring constantly until sauce thickens slightly. Adjust seasoning.
Return chicken to the sauce. Serve immediately with roasted potatoes and sautéed mushrooms & bell pepper. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Use high-quality Hungarian paprika for authentic flavor and vibrant color.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Ricotta Ravioli with Caramelized Onion Jam and Spiced Savory Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of delicate, handmade sweet ricotta ravioli, precisely cut into large squares, is artfully arranged on a clean white porcelain plate. The ravioli are plump, showcasing their smooth, pale yellow pasta casing. Each piece is lightly glossed with a transparent, sweet butter sauce. A small, artful dollop of deep amber, intensely caramelized onion jam rests beside the ravioli, offering a rich, contrasting color and texture. Scattered sparingly over and around the ravioli is a fine, golden-brown crumble made from finely minced, pan-fried sweet sausage and sautéed mushrooms, subtly spiced with cinnamon and nutmeg. This crumble provides a textural contrast and a hint of unexpected savory depth. The plate maintains moderate negative space, emphasizing the clean lines of the ravioli and the refined presentation. A crisp white linen napkin and silver flatware are placed beside the plate on a simple wooden surface, under soft, natural lighting, creating a modern bistro ambiance.

ingredients.name: Mild pork sausage (e.g., breakfast sausage), casings removed

instructions: Prepare sweet pasta dough: On a clean surface, combine flour and granulated sugar. Make a well in the center. Crack eggs into the well. Whisk eggs with a fork, gradually incorporating flour. Knead dough 10-12 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in cling film. Rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.

Make caramelized onion jam: Thinly slice onions. Melt 15 g butter in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deep golden brown and very soft. Stir in brown sugar and balsamic vinegar. Cook 5 more minutes until liquid evaporates and jam is thick. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside to cool.
Prepare sweet ricotta filling: In a bowl, combine ricotta, powdered sugar, lemon zest, and vanilla bean paste. Mix until smooth and creamy. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired. Cover and chill.

Make spiced savory crumble: In a separate pan, cook sausage over medium heat, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat. Add finely minced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and are tender. Stir in maple syrup, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Cook 2 minutes. Stir in panko breadcrumbs. Cook until breadcrumbs are lightly toasted and mixture is crumbly. Set aside.

Assemble ravioli: Divide pasta dough into four portions. Working with one portion at a time, roll dough very thinly using a pasta machine or rolling pin. Lay a sheet of pasta on a lightly floured surface. Place small spoonfuls (about 10 g each) of ricotta filling, spaced 4 cm apart, on one half of the pasta sheet. Top each ricotta portion with a tiny dab (about 2 g) of caramelized onion jam. Fold the other half of the pasta sheet over the filling. Gently press around each mound to seal, expelling air. Cut into 4 cm squares using a fluted pasta wheel or knife. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
Cook ravioli: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a gentle boil. Carefully add ravioli in batches. Cook 3-4 minutes until they float and are tender. Do not overcrowd the pot.

Finish and plate: Melt remaining 15 g butter in a small pan. Drain cooked ravioli. Gently toss with melted butter. Arrange 4-5 ravioli per plate. Spoon a small amount of remaining caramelized onion jam beside the ravioli. Sprinkle the spiced savory crumble sparingly over and around the ravioli. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Black-Eyed Pea Salad with Grilled Chicken and Lamb
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Black-Eyed Pea Salad is presented on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, set on a well-used, warm wooden dining table.
